patterns.what_worked: The relationship, not the data: a GRADED table's drill must change its verdict when that table is mutated and must NOT change when ANOTHER class's table is mutated (the cross-isolation half). The plans (the due opener, the pull moments, the press) are computed ONCE from the pristine table, so a mutation changes the verdict instead of silently following the mutated data. The CITATION half is proved by a whole-tree symbol scan with comments AND string bodies blanked (a mention in prose is not a reader) plus the marker in the comment block above the declaration. Every scan carries a floor so an empty scan cannot pass as evidence.
patterns.what_was_hard: The brief's paladin clause does not match the tree: `paladin_prepull` grades the class's own file-local per-order SEAL SPEC, not the published `ST.PALADIN.practice_prepull_rows` (which has no consumer anywhere). Rather than write a false assertion, the suite asserts the truth - the drill follows the class's own per-order spec (two orders with different seals grade differently) and the published rows table is the marked citation layer. Also: Lua 5.1 has no `__len`, so a read-trap cannot proxy an array - the lateness-band tables are proved by mutation instead of a proxy.
patterns.skill_gap: A brief that lists four drill keys and then says 'a class with NO pre-pull drill must be marked citation-only' can be internally inconsistent; the resolution was to check the tree (whole-tree symbol scan) and then assert the tree's truth, filing the divergence as a residual for an operator ruling instead of bending a test to the prose.
